co_cathedral_wall.blurb: Cathedral Wall is a tall alpine face at the head of Loch Vale in Rocky Mountain National Park, well above 10,000 feet. Nearly all of its 15 climbs are long alpine trad lines, six to eight pitches on the main and second buttresses, mostly 5.9 and 5.10 with a couple at 5.11. Many are serious and bold, though a few moderate lines exist. The face catches early light and glows orange in the morning. Plan a committed day: weather can turn fast at this elevation, and the walk off the top is involved and easy to misjudge.
co_cathedral_wall.parking_note: Leave the car at the Glacier Gorge trailhead lot, then hike toward Sky Pond.
co_cathedral_wall.approach: Hike the Sky Pond trail to just beyond the Andrews Glacier junction, then leave it and cross talus slopes to the base of the wall.

co_north_side.blurb: North Side is the back face of Bird Rock, in the West Creek part of the South Platte at roughly 8,500 feet. The walls are steep and mostly shaded, with sun gone by late morning, which makes this a good summer refuge. Of its 15 climbs, nine are sport and six trad, and the difficulty runs high: most lines fall between 5.12 and 5.13, with only a few easier options around 5.9 to 5.11. The granite is clean and solid. Getting here means hiking around the formation with a fair amount of boulder hopping.

co_black_see.blurb: Black See is a granite dome at about 8,700 feet in the Ironclads near Allenspark, a few minutes on foot across the valley from the Ironsides wall. Its 15 routes, nine trad and six sport, run from 5.7 up to 5.12, with the bulk at 5.10 and 5.11. Most lines sit on the west and north faces and include bolted slabs and roofs, while a short tunnel on the northeast side stays in shade. To reach the back side, scramble through the tunnel at the east end or circle the west end and climb the gully behind.

co_bullet_hole_cliff_band.blurb: Bullet Hole Cliff Band is a short band of rock above Monument Road near Grand Junction, at about 4,800 feet and just uphill of the Bullet Hole boulders. Of its 15 climbs, ten are trad, with a few sport lines, one top rope and one boulder problem, ranging from easy 5.5 climbs to a couple at 5.11. The routes are short, so it suits beginners, skills practice and quick laps close to town. Top-roping generally means building your own anchors, and the hillside leading up is steep and loose.
co_bullet_hole_cliff_band.approach: Hike straight up the steep, loose hillside above the lower boulders, or follow the trail that runs left past the main boulders.

co_first_wall.blurb: First Wall is the first section you meet at Hurd Creek Crag, a single-pitch outcrop near Fraser in Grand County, at about 9,000 feet. Of its 15 climbs, 13 are bolted sport routes and two are trad, running from easy 5.4 and 5.6 lines up to 5.11 and 5.12, with most between 5.7 and 5.10. The crag as a whole is gneiss with a southwest tilt, so it tends to be sunny and warm. On the walk in, keep to the right when the trail forks.

co_permission_wall.blurb: Permission Wall is a large buttress at Meadow Dome in Staunton Rocks, Staunton State Park, southwest of Denver at about 8,900 feet, and the first wall you reach at the dome. Of 15 climbs, nine are sport, five trad and one top rope, nearly all between 5.9 and 5.11 with the bulk at 5.9 and 5.10. Routes can be finished after one pitch at a broad ledge with a rappel anchor, or continued to the dome's top. It is a solid choice for mid-grade bolted and gear lines.

co_marmot_tower.blurb: Marmot Tower is a small formation high on the hillside above the Dungeon in Staunton Rocks, Staunton State Park, near 8,900 feet. It holds 15 climbs, seven sport, six trad and two top rope, from 5.5 up to about 5.11, with most at 5.8 and 5.9 and a few gentle options for newer leaders. The walk in is the longest and steepest of any crag in the park, so the tower sees fewer visitors than the lower walls. Expect a quiet, scenic spot with a limited but varied selection.

co_gill_boulder_the.blurb: The Gill Boulder is a big, blocky boulder in Eldorado Canyon State Park near Boulder, beside a shady picnic area at the canyon's final bridge. Problems line every side, 15 in all, mostly V0 to V4 with a pair at V6 and two very hard double-digit lines. Many are long-standing classics. The lower holds are polished from heavy traffic, so easier problems can feel slick and stiffer than their grade. It is a social spot that draws groups, so bring several pads and spotters.
co_gill_boulder_the.parking_note: Use the picnic area lot at the canyon's final bridge; the boulder stands a few steps from the parked cars.

_conflicts.co_cathedral_wall: Stored rock is 'metamorphic rock' but https://app.advcollective.com/climbing/cathedral-wall-colorados-alpine-climbing-giant calls it solid granite; blurb names no rock.
